title: An inbound email claims a pull request shipped that never actually merged
author: off-by-one
description: The twelfth leg of the claims-unmerged-pr family, and the third recipe to read gmail: the Gmail-side twin of mention-claims-unmerged-pr (the X-mention leg), slack-message-claims-unmerged-pr (the Slack-channel leg), and linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr (the Linear-comment leg) -- the same 'twin the inbound siblings, not the town-controlled ones' shape email-claims-unfixed-issue already drew for the claims-unfixed-issue family. Extracts every ships/includes/merges/via #N claim (the shared seam_engine.pr_claims grammar eleven sibling recipes already import) from an inbound email's own body and cross-checks it against the live pull-request tracker's own state -- a status-update email sitting in a connected inbox is exactly as durable and readable-later as a tweet, a mention, a Slack message, or a Linear comment, and nothing on either platform ever compares it against the PR tracker's real state. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the email's own received_at, holding mention-claims-unmerged-pr's/slack-message-claims-unmerged-pr's/linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's identical 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the toolkit is new. A claim checked within 24 hours of the email landing might still be a race (the real merge landing moments after the email went out) rather than a settled overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named PR still unmerged, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-unmerged-pr sibling: the claimed PR's own live state/merged fields, verified against ListPullRequests, not a guess about which tracker the sender meant. A named PR that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- that broken reference is email-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's. A named PR that IS merged is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. An email with no claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the sender -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
